pains.title: PPO write-offs and production that never match the bank
pains.problem: Your practice reports show production and your bank shows deposits. The gap is PPO write-offs, unpaid claims and patient balances, and most books bury it.
pains.how: Lucid reconciles production and collections to your bank deposits each month, then reports revenue by plan: billed, allowed and written off. You decide what to renegotiate.

pains.title: Cash that arrives weeks after the work
pains.problem: Insurance pays on a lag, so a practice can look profitable on paper and still be short two days before payroll.
pains.how: Your biller still handles claims. Lucid does not file, appeal or chase them. It puts your bank balance, payments and write-offs in one cash forecast.

pains.title: Several offices, one blended number
pains.problem: One blended P&L hides which office carries the others. Shared staff, lab spend and management fees move between entities unreconciled.
pains.how: Lucid reports each office and builds one combined owner view, with intercompany reconciliation for management fees. You see live P&L and margin by location.

cta: Book a free 30 minute consult. Bring your last P&L and your practice reports, and Lucid will show you where the numbers drift. Terms are month to month.

faq.q: How should I measure dental practice overhead?
faq.a: Pick one yardstick and use it every month. Some sources compare costs to collections and others to production, and some include owner pay. Lucid tracks every cost line the same way each month, so if overhead is rising faster than production you can see which line moved and act on that one first.

faq.q: Why does my P&L not match what my practice software says I produced?
faq.a: Production is the value of the dentistry you did before write-offs. Your books record the money that actually arrived. The gap is insurance write-offs, unpaid claims and patient balances. Lucid reconciles insurance claims, PPO write-offs and patient payments every month so you can see what happened to the difference.

faq.q: Why is my dental practice short on cash when production looks great?
faq.a: Insurance often pays weeks after the work, and part of what you produce is never collected. Lucid puts your bank balance next to insurance and patient payments and builds a cash forecast so payroll weeks are not a surprise. Your biller still handles the claims themselves.

faq.q: How do I see which of my dental offices is making money?
faq.a: Each office needs its own books set up the same way, with shared costs split on a clear rule. Lucid reports P&L and margin by location or provider plus a combined owner view, with intercompany reconciliation for management fees and money moving between entities. That shows which office is carrying the others.

faq.q: Can I write off a new CBCT or milling machine?
faq.a: Equipment can sometimes be deducted in the first year through Section 179 or bonus depreciation, depending on current rules and your income. Timing and how you pay for it matter, so review it before you sign. Lucid models what the purchase does to your tax bill and your cash, and your CPA confirms the rules.
